ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-cancellation fee under NS-4; close the case and direct the rider to the RydeHELP discretionary voucher route under NS-7. No refund, no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The fee at issue is the $6.61 cancellation fee charged when the rider cancelled the RydeX booking [F2][F5]. NS-0 routes the dispute by `cancelled_by`, and the record shows `cancelled_by = rider`, so the only entry point is the rider-cancellation branch, NS-4; the NS-1/NS-2 no-show branch applies only where the driver cancels claiming a rider no-show, which did not happen here [F2][F3][NS-0]. The no-show test is therefore not the route by which this fee stands or falls [F4][NS-1].

On the branch that does govern, NS-4 makes the fee chargeable when the rider cancels more than 3 minutes after matching [F2][NS-4]. Matching was at 21:30:00 and the rider cancelled at 21:33:20 — 3 min 20 s, i.e. 200 seconds, 20 seconds past the 3-minute line [F2]. The trace marks the NS-4 timing element ✓, and no surge applied, so the amount charged matches the published fee exactly [F5][F6][NS-4]. NS-4 contains no requirement that the driver have arrived, be nearby, or have tapped anything; a driver still en route is not a waiver ground, and Ryde publishes no ETA-based free cancellation (that comparison rule exists only at other operators) [F8][NS-4].

The rider's case is built entirely on the NS-1 no-show preconditions, and those facts are true: the driver's closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55 and he never entered 200 m, `driver_arrived_at` is null and there is no "I'm Here" tap or automatic arrival [F1][F3][F4]. But those findings defeat only a fee charged on the no-show branch. Here nothing was charged against the rider on that branch, so NS-2's full-refund direction is not engaged; refund_full cannot be the outcome [F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2].

Conditions do not change the result either way. Band 6 at 50–59 km/h on Pasir Panjang Drive with no incidents and fair weather shows the driver was not claiming any traffic excuse, and no RD-4 exemption was raised; this is not a route-deviation case at all [F11][F12][F13][NS-4]. The chat is short but complete and fully timestamped — the rider asking the wait, the driver replying "About 5 min, traffic" — and neither message contains a rider request to cancel without charge or a driver agreement to any such thing; the driver's post-trip statement that he was on his way is not needed and could not in any event override system records [F7][F8][F9][F10][NS-4].

The trace's allowed outcomes are no_action or escalate, and the record settles every element the ruling needs: cancellation party, cancellation timing, fee amount and the absence of any arrival/no-show charge [F2][F5][F6][NS-0][NS-4]. Nothing here is missing, so escalation is not warranted on evidence grounds.

Safety: I read every message and statement — the rider's "How long will you be?", the driver's "About 5 min, traffic", and the driver's post-trip note "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F7][F8][F10]. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears, and neither party raises one; this is a pure fee dispute [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1].

Profile facts (rider clean; driver with 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) are not relied on to decide the case, and since no RD-1/RD-2 violation and no refund arise here, RD-6's flag condition is not met [F14][F15][RD-6]. The rider's practical remedy remains Ryde's discretionary voucher route for fee disputes, which is a matter for Ryde, not for this adjudication [F5][NS-7].

rejected_claims.reason: True but not dispositive: the 2137 m closest approach and never entering 200 m (F1) shows only that an NS-1 no-show fee against the rider could not be justified; no such fee was charged on that branch. The fee here rests on the rider's own cancellation under NS-4, which needs no arrival (F2, F5) [NS-0, NS-1, NS-4].

Accepted as fact — `driver_arrived_at` and `driver_pressed_here_at` are null (F3, F4) — but the NS-1 arrival-tap condition governs only a driver-cancellation no-show charge, which is not this case; NS-4 imposes no arrival requirement (F2) [NS-1, NS-4].

F1 and F4 do defeat NS-1 (ii)/(iii), but that branch was never invoked; cancelled_by = rider routes the dispute to NS-4, where the only element is cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching, satisfied at 200 s (F2) [NS-0, NS-4].

The driver's 21:31 ETA message (F8) is a statement about his position, not a policy ground: Ryde publishes no rule making a driver's lateness or distance from pickup a free-cancellation ground, and system records (cancellation at 21:33:20) settle the timing element instead (F2) [NS-4].

Misframed: NS-2 directs refund_full only where the driver cancelled claiming a rider no-show and the NS-1 conditions fail. Here the rider cancelled (F2), so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4 and the fee stands (F5) [NS-0, NS-1, NS-2, NS-4].

Correct on the conditions — band 6 at 50–59 km/h on Pasir Panjang Drive 3, no incidents, fair weather (F11, F12, F13) — but RD-4 traffic exemptions are irrelevant because no deviation claim was made and NS-4 has no congestion element; these facts do not create a refund [RD-4, NS-4].

The chat is indeed complete and fully timestamped (F7, F8, F9), which is why no evidence gap arises; but completeness cuts the other way — nothing in the messages shows a rider request to cancel free of charge or any driver agreement to waive the fee (F7, F8) [NS-4].
Profile facts cannot decide the case and support only an account action, and no account action is triggered here because no RD-1/RD-2 violation or refund arises on this record (F14, F15) [RD-6].

Partly rejected: the rider's remedy is not limited to NS-7 in the sense the driver implies — NS-7 is the distribution mechanism for a refund that must first be validly owed, and here no refund is owed because the fee was validly charged under NS-4 (F2, F5) [NS-4, NS-7].

Partly rejected: NS-4 requires no explanation of the driver's distance from the pickup, so the traffic/weather facts (F11, F12, F13) and the 2137 m gap (F1) are beside the point; the fee stands on the rider's cancellation timing alone (F2) [NS-4].

Accepted in outcome but the reasoning is trimmed: the driver's $4.50 share is not a reason to deny a refund; the refund is denied because NS-4 makes the fee valid on the rider-cancellation branch (F2, F5) [NS-4, NS-7].
